hints.title: Greedy Ordering
hints.text: Sorting the array allows greedy assignment of the smallest possible distinct integer to each number.

hints.title: Interval Bounds
hints.text: Each element num can become any integer in the closed interval [num - k, num + k].

hints.title: Next Available Assignment
hints.text: Track the next available unused integer and assign max(num - k, next_available) when within range.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maxDistinctElements(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        nums.sort()
        next_available = -float('inf')
        distinct_count = 0
        
        for num in nums:
            left = num - k
            right = num + k
            target = max(left, next_available)
            if target <= right:
                distinct_count += 1
                next_available = target + 1
                
        return distinct_count
```

complexity.notes: Sorting takes O(n log n) followed by a linear greedy assignment scan.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Arbitrary assignment without sorting risks blocking future elements needlessly.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(1) auxiliary space beyond the in-place sort.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Sorts input and demonstrates greedy invariant preserving maximum room for subsequent values.
